newsitem.title: USA: National Semi sees deal dilutive in Q3, Q4.
newsitem.headline: National Semi sees deal dilutive in Q3, Q4.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp expects its acquisition of Cyrix Corp to dilute its earnings per share in the third and fourth quarters of its current fiscal year, but said it will be accretive after that, company executives said.

Chief Financial Officer Donald Macleod said National Semiconductor would issue an additional 16 million shares as the merger deal with Cyrix is completed and those additional shares -- which will boost the full share count of the combined company by about 10 percent -- would effectively dilute earnings per share at first.

"We are making broad assumptions that in the third and fourth quarters -- the February and May quarters of National's current fiscal year -- that, conservatively, the Cyrix business will be a break-even business and therefore will be dilutive to the extent of the extra shares outstanding," Macleod said.

"Beyond that, we see benefits coming in through the summer of next year as we try to integrate our business plans to produce new products that will add to the earnings of the combined corporation," he said. "We expect that to bring accretive results going forward into fiscal 1999."

National Semiconductor Chief Executive Officer Brian Halla said the combined company would focus on providing "system-on-a-chip solutions" enabling manufacturers to send sub-$500 personal computers into the marketplace.
"Now it is truly possible to enable computing and the information age to reach the masses," Halla said.
"Where do we go from enabling a sub-$500 personal computer? We enable a sub-$200 PC and other low-cost information appliances," he said.

Jay Swent, acting chief executive of Cyrix, said the combined company's focus on providing for cheaper personal computers did not mean it was giving up on the high-end market, where it has produced the so-called 6x86MX chip to compete with Intel's Pentium MMX multimedia chip but has had trouble breaking Intel's dominance.

"Cyrix's strategy is to participate significantly in mid-range PC markets with the 6x86MX and to dominate the entry-level, sub-$1000 PC market with our integrated Media GX processor," Swent told analysts during the conference call.

"We are definitely not abandoning the high-end, high-performance 6x86MX kind of processor ... We are 100 percent committed to having at all times, with very few exceptions, a leading edge, high-end performance processor in the portfolio and we'll continue to invest there," he said.
